# Use a standard Ubuntu LTS version as the base image
# This provides a stable and well-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variable to prevent interactive prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none: Disables a shared-memory optimization that can cause issues in containers.
# OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=yes: Allows MPI processes to be bound to the same core, which is common in oversubscribed Kubernetes nodes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=yes

# Set the default working directory for subsequent commands
WORKDIR /app

# Combine installation, build, and cleanup into a single RUN layer to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    fftw3-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    ca-certificates \
    # FIX: Add python3, a required dependency for the LAMMPS cmake build process
    python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code from GitHub
    && git clone https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /lammps \
    # As per instructions, copy example files for the reaxff/HNS benchmark into the WORKDIR
    && cp /lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* . \
    # Create a build directory and navigate into it
    && cd /lammps && mkdir build && cd build \
    # Configure the LAMMPS build using CMake
    # -D PKG_REAXFF=on: Enables the ReaxFF package required for the simulation
    && cmake -D PKG_REAXFF=on ../cmake \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    # Copy the compiled LAMMPS executable 'lmp' to a system path
    && cp lmp /usr/local/bin/ \
    # Clean up the source code directory to minimize final image size
    && rm -rf /lammps

# Set a default command to run the LAMMPS executable with a typical input file for the copied example
CMD ["lmp", "-in", "in.hns"]

# MiniCluster manifest for a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation on a single node.
# API Version v1alpha2 is used as required for the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deployment will be in the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Specify the number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # For a single-node run, this is set to 1.
  size: 1

  # Total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # This is inferred from the lmp command arguments (-v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -> 2*2*2=8).
  # The Flux Operator will wrap the command with `flux run -n 8 ...`.
  tasks: 8

  # Enable strict validation for the MiniCluster spec.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Per instructions, do not automatically clean up the job pods upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Define the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute the LAMMPS simulation.
      # This will be run inside the container's working directory.
      # The Flux Operator automatically prepends `flux run`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is a worker, not a launcher-only pod.
      launcher: false

      # Tells the operator that this container's command should be run under `flux`.
      runFlux: true

      # No resource requests or limits are set, allowing the pod to be
      # scheduled as BestEffort and use available node resources.
